title: How Silver Leaf differed from Tuxedo; quadrilles and blues
summary: Tuxedo had better arrangements and practice; Silver Leaf played straight music, quadrilles were gone, and blues were played.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Well I was wondering the difference. Did the Silver Leaf sound much different than the... Original Tuxedo? Original Tuxedo? Oh.
What was the difference? Did they play different kind of music?
But the men could just... But we all had to improve. Even myself.
Yeah sure you'd improve. I wondered though.

And then we had different ideas you know. Better ideas. You know how to make different own arrangements like that and practicing. And we used to get to... Oh Graff one I believe we called it you know. And something come out like that where the other bands would be playing. But we would just have a practice like that. We called it special practice when we had one fella playing a clarinet named Ezebri Zanaris. Lana Rees. And he could catch those records. He played C clarinet. And he could catch those records. No, not that time it was gone. We didn't play. It's gone already. Yeah, now if we, we have played quadrilles for different dancers like that, special dancers, but the people would ask for them and we just get some boots and practice them up, you know. But that wouldn't, we didn't use that in no way as else. But that was always gone. But when we come along during the Charleston time, we could play that. We could play the Charleston days.
Did the Silver Leaf ever play blues much? Yeah. They played blues too. They played blues.
Or they had to do it. Yes. See, they had to play some kind of blues.
